subject: Re: ClarusAI onboarding — model shortlist, context needs & hourly token projection
messages:
From: Eleanor Dawson <eleanor@clarusrx.ai>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clarusrx.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ClarusAI onboarding — initial traffic sample and context questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency profile. Per our conversation, attaching a small weekly sample of API events so you can start sizing. A few things we want to lock down during kickoff:

- Preferred model family for conversational summaries (short customer support transcripts, avg 400 tokens).
- Context needs for multi-turn threads (we typically send 6–12 turns, sometimes include metadata + last 2 messages as system prompt).
- Peak-hour QPS: the attached sample has hourly buckets, but we see occasional spikes up to ~85 requests/hour in the 11–14 PST window.

Can you draft an initial model shortlist and a ballpark hourly token projection (p50/p95) for our pilot (500k monthly tokens baseline, with 20% peak headroom)? Would like to share with the product owner before the kickoff next week.

Attachments: clarus_weekly_traffic_sample.csv (csv)

—Eleanor
Eleanor Dawson | Head of Product, ClarusRx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClarusAI onboarding — initial traffic sample and context questions

Eleanor — thanks for the sample, that helped. Sharing initial read and a proposed shortlist below; attaching a one-page summary (mina_model_recs_v1.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_draft.md).

High-level answers first:
- Typical convo patterns: 400 token transcripts + 80 token system + 2-turn history => ~880 tokens/request median.
- Peak window sizing: your 85 rph spike translates to ~75 concurrent short-lived requests at peak for throughput planning (assuming avg 3s server-side processing).

Proposed model shortlist (pilot):
1) llama-33b-int8 (Redwood-verified): good balance for instruction-following; expect ~1.6× cost vs smaller quantized variants but better output quality for long context.
2) vicuna-13b-4bit (quantized): strong cost profile for single-turn summarization where hallucination risk is low; recommended for non-critical summary pass.
3) redwood-mini-chat-7b-q4: lowest cost option, ideal for embedding and lightweight routing decisions (e.g., intent classify, short-format rephrases).

Context length recommendations:
- Primary route (default): 2,048 token window (covers 6–12 turn history + metadata).
- Fallback short route: 1,024 tokens for latency-critical requests or when we detect low-value history.

Ballpark hourly token projection (pilot, 30-day look):
- Baseline: 500k tokens/month => ~16.7k tokens/day => ~700 tokens/hour average.
- With your observed peaks (20% headroom) adjust to p50 ~850 tokens/hour, p95 ~7,500 tokens/hour (during the 11–14 PST multi-hour spike).

Operational notes / asks:
- Monica: can you confirm whether ClarusRx will include user PII in the system prompt? If so we need to propose an isolated routing plan + consent flags.
- Priyom: can your team prepare a short eval prompt set (10 transcripts) to validate quality tradeoffs between 13b and 33b variants?

Next steps (for kickoff):
- Share final shortlist with product owner by EOD Friday.
- We’ll provide cost delta estimates for the three candidates and a suggested canary rollout (10% traffic -> 50% -> full).

Attachments: mina_model_recs_v1.pdf (summary), mutual_action_plan_draft.md (draft MAP)

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@clarusrx.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Eleanor Dawson <eleanor@clarusrx.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClarusAI onboarding — initial traffic sample and context questions

Thanks Mina, this is helpful. Quick clarifications:
- We do strip direct PII fields (SSNs, full DOBs) from transcripts upstream but keep names and customer IDs — safe to assume names remain in the history.
- For the eval set, we'll prepare 12 transcripts and flag 3 that are intentionally noisy (bad ASR) to test robustness.

One small ask on routing: during peak hours we'd prefer the 13b-quantized path to handle non-critical summaries and reserve 33b for agent-assist flows. Is that something you can reflect in the MAP?

Subject: Re: ClarusAI onboarding — initial traffic sample and context questions

Samir / Eleanor — thanks for the clarifications, that routing preference makes sense. Updated plan below and next steps to lock for kickoff.

Updated shortlist + routing:
- Default routing: vicuna-13b-4bit for non-agent summaries and bulk nightly jobs.
- Canary / agent-assist: llama-33b-int8 for agent-facing flows and high-value responses.
- Edge tasks (intent, classification): redwood-mini-chat-7b-q4.

Revised hourly token projection (with sample + noisy transcripts):
- Pilot baseline p50: 1,000 tokens/hour (small increase due to noisy re-requests).
- Pilot p95: 8,200 tokens/hour (assumes multi-hour spike + retries).
- Concurrency estimate at p95: ~120 concurrent requests (planning for 3s avg inference time), recommend reserving dedicated burst capacity for the 11–14 PST window.

Mutual Action Plan items (summary):
1) ClarusRx provides eval set (12 transcripts) — due 2026-09-07.
2) Redwood runs quality benchmark between vicuna-13b-4bit and llama-33b-int8 — deliverable 2026-09-10.
3) Cost delta report + canary rollout plan (10%/50%/100%) — deliverable 2026-09-11.
4) Technical kickoff (network + keys + test endpoints) — target 2026-09-14.

Attachments included: mutual_action_plan_draft.md (with the timeline above). Monica will be owner for the benchmark and Priyom will configure the routing policies in Redwood Console.

Monica / Priyom — can you confirm you’re ok owning those items and I’ll update the HubSpot record? Also tagging a short note on isolation: because names remain in payloads, we should propose a soft-PII classification tag that triggers audit logs and retention policy 90 days for the pilot.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the MAP and send the kickoff invite.

Best — Mina
Mina Haddad | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
